graphs.title: The acceleration rises in a straight line as the force rises.
graphs.label: Acceleration

sentences: Try a mass of 2 kg and then 10 kg at the same force.
title: Newton's second law: force, mass and acceleration
goal: Explore how the acceleration of an object depends on the resultant force and the mass.
note: The acceleration of an object is the resultant force divided by its mass: a = F / m. A bigger force gives a bigger acceleration, and a bigger mass gives a smaller acceleration.

predict.prompt: If the resultant force stays the same and the mass doubles, what happens to the acceleration?
predict.reveal: Hold the force at its starting value and compare the mass at 2 kg with 4 kg.

hints: Write down the formula: acceleration = force / mass.
Put the force in newtons and the mass in kilograms.
Divide the force by the mass.
worked_solution: Write the formula: a = F / m.
Substitute the resultant force and the mass.
Divide to get the acceleration in m/s2.
